name: Anse Chastanet
positioning: Eco-resort on a 600-acre estate on St. Lucia's south-west coast, with two beaches, a protected reef offshore and individually designed rooms facing the Pitons
best_for: Divers and snorkelers who want a reef just off the beach
Couples who want open-air rooms with Piton and sea views
Active travelers who want biking and hiking trails on the estate

facts.text: Anse Chastanet sits on a private estate of 600 tropical acres and borders two soft-sand Caribbean beaches.
The estate is a gateway to the Pitons, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and fronts two bays within a designated marine reserve that protects coral reefs.
Anse Chastanet was created by architect and owner Nick Troubetzkoy.
Room furniture is individually designed and handmade in the region from island woods such as teak, mahogany, green heart, red cedar and wild breadfruit.
Cushions and bedspreads are made from madras, the island's national cloth.
Premium rooms sit on the higher hillside level, with views of the Pitons and the Caribbean Sea.
Beachside deluxe rooms have a tropical garden view and are just a few feet from the beach and the water's edge.
The Anse Chastanet reef begins just steps from the shoreline.
Yoga is held daily, morning and evening, in the beach gazebo.
Complimentary non-motorized water sports include snorkel gear, windsurfers, sit-on-top kayaks, Sunfish sailing and paddle boarding.
The Treehouse Restaurant serves dinner in two open-air treehouses overlooking tropical foliage and the Caribbean Sea.
The Sulphur Springs, the Louis XVI Mineral Baths, the rainforest and the Pitons are all within a short distance of the resort.

highlights.text: In one suite the balcony is built around a full-grown red gommier tree, and some suites have their fourth wall open entirely to the views while remaining private.
Octagonal whitewashed cottages have wraparound flower-draped balconies and louvered windows to make the most of the views and the tradewinds.
Guests can explore the resort's coral nursery with one of its marine biologists.
The resort has 12 miles of jungle biking, walking and hiking trails in the Anse Mamin valley, with birdwatching.
Kai Belte Spa offers massages, Ayurvedic rituals and chocolate-focused treatments such as a chocolate facial and mocha massage.

considerations.text: There are approximately 100 stairs from beach level to mid-hillside level, making the property unsuitable for those with walking difficulties or cardiac problems.
The resort is an hour's drive or a six-minute helicopter ride from Hewanorra International Airport.
WhataHotel notes that some rooms have no air conditioning and rely on natural ventilation.
